key_insight: Quantum impurity solvers could help screen strongly correlated oxygen-electrode materials, but quantum advantage remains to be demonstrated.
engineering_relevance: The framework links atomic-scale electrode properties to solid oxide fuel cell and electrolyser performance, enabling assessment of potential engineering and business value.
method: Use DFT screening to shortlist materials and construct correlated impurity models from electrode–electrolyte interfaces.
Combine GW+DMFT or SEET embedding with quantum-computed finite-temperature impurity Green’s functions.
Connect vacancy energetics and electronic conductivity to continuum electrode models and deployment scenarios.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports illustrative logical-qubit counts and scenario-based value estimates, while specifying convergence tests and classical-solver comparisons needed to assess quantum advantage.
watch_item: A complete resource assessment must include thermal-state preparation, simulation, measurement, and repeated impurity solves—not just logical-qubit counts.
paper_title: Screening strongly correlated materials in solid oxide cells with quantum simulation
